report.summary: The change merges the three Vitest invocations into one run with three projects (worker, ui, components), runs the UI and component projects on vmThreads with two workers each, and runs the workspace-events Worker cases concurrently (maxConcurrency 4) with test-context expect. Each concurrent case seeds its own user, project, workspace and Durable Object, so cases do not share fixtures. Each case keeps its timeout, including the it.for stop-reason cases, which now pass { timeout: T }. The worker config moved unchanged apart from name and maxConcurrency. tsconfig and docs/CI.md are updated, and Turborepo's default inputs cover the new config files. Nothing blocks the merge; the notes are about checking timing and flakiness. This review only read the code and did not run the test suite.

findings.text: CLAUDE.md says a change to the test suite must report the relevant stage timing from the CI summary. The diff has no before/after timing for the merged Vitest run or for the four-way concurrency, so it does not show the change helps or stays within the 270 s budget. Add the timings to the PR description.

maxConcurrency 4 with maxWorkers 2 lets up to 8 Durable Object cases run at once in workerd. The helpers still use fixed wall-clock deadlines (waitFor and applied at 5000 ms, driveUntil polling alarms), so these deadlines get tighter under contention and may flake on a slow CI runner. Run the suite several times on CI to confirm it is stable, or scale the test-only deadlines.

seedWorkspace reads the module-level seedCounter after seedProject has awaited D1. With concurrent cases, two workspaces can get the same default slug (city<N>). This is harmless now because the unique index workspaces_active_slug is scoped by project_id and every case seeds its own project. A later test that reuses a project across concurrent cases would hit a uniqueness error. Consider taking the slug from the counter value seedProject captured, or from newId().
